column1: 1:1|The vision Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.|Preserve prophet, father, geography, four kings.

1:2|Hear, heavens! Listen, earth!
The **LORD** has spoken:
“I raised children and brought them up,
but they rebelled against me.|Retain cosmic summons and parental accusation.

1:3|An ox knows its owner,
a donkey its master’s feeding trough,
but Israel does not know;
my people do not understand.”|Preserve two animals and knowing refrain.

1:4|Alas, sinful nation,
people weighed down with guilt,
offspring of evildoers, corrupt children!
They have abandoned the **LORD**,
scorned the Holy One of Israel,
and turned their backs.|Retain family indictment and Holy One title.

1:5|Why invite more blows?
Why keep rebelling?
The whole head is sick,
the whole heart faint.|Keep bodily metaphor and questions.

1:6|From the sole of the foot to the head,
no part is sound—
wounds, bruises, raw sores,
not cleaned, not bandaged,
not soothed with oil.|Retain untreated injuries and three negatives.

1:8|Daughter Zion is left
like a shelter in a vineyard,
a hut in a cucumber field,
a city under siege.|Preserve daughter personification and three similes.
1:9|Had the **LORD** of hosts not left us a few survivors,\nwe would have become like Sodom,\nlike Gomorrah.|Retain remnant and named cities.
1:10|Hear the **LORD**’s word, rulers of Sodom!\nListen to our God’s instruction, people of Gomorrah!|Preserve accusatory renamed audience and instruction.

1:11|“What do I want with all your sacrifices?” says the **LORD**.
“I have had enough burnt offerings of rams
and the fat of well-fed animals.
I take no pleasure in the blood
of bulls, lambs, or male goats.|Keep complete sacrificial animal list.
1:12|When you come to appear before me,\nwho asked you to trample my courts?|Retain presence and trampling question.

1:13|Bring no more empty offerings!
Your incense disgusts me.
New moons, Sabbaths, summoned assemblies—
I cannot bear wrongdoing joined to solemn gatherings.|Preserve ritual terms and ethical conjunction.
1:14|I hate your new moons and appointed festivals.\nThey have become a burden;\nI am tired of carrying them.|Retain divine hatred and burden imagery.

1:15|When you spread out your hands,
I will hide my eyes from you.
Even if you multiply prayers, I will not listen.
Your hands are full of blood.|Keep prayer posture and bloody hands.
1:16|Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean.\nRemove your evil deeds from my sight.\nStop doing evil.|Retain bodily washing and ethical commands.

1:17|Learn to do good. Seek justice.
Set oppression right.
Defend the fatherless;
plead the widow’s case.|Keep distinct legal actions and difficult oppression phrase.

1:18|“Come now, let us settle the matter,” says the **LORD**.
“Though your sins are scarlet,
they shall be white as snow;
though red as crimson,
they shall become like wool.|Preserve judicial invitation and two color contrasts.
1:19|If you are willing and listen,\nyou will eat the land’s good produce.|Retain conditional willing obedience and eating.
1:20|But if you refuse and rebel,\nthe sword will eat you.”\nThe mouth of the **LORD** has spoken.|Keep eat/be-eaten wordplay and closing authority.

1:21|How the faithful city has become a prostitute!
Once she was full of justice;
righteousness lodged in her—
but now, murderers.|Retain sexual city metaphor and lodging contrast.
1:22|Your silver has become dross;\nyour drink is diluted with water.|Keep two adulterated substances.

1:23|Your rulers are rebels, partners of thieves.
Every one loves a bribe and chases rewards.
They do not defend the fatherless;
the widow’s case never reaches them.|Preserve systemic corruption and excluded litigants.

1:24|Therefore the Lord, the **LORD** of hosts,
the Mighty One of Israel, declares:
“Ah, I will find relief from my adversaries
and take vengeance on my enemies.|Retain three divine titles and vengeance.
1:25|I will turn my hand against you,\nsmelt away your dross as with lye,\nand remove all your alloy.|Keep purification as hostile hand and metallurgy.

1:26|I will restore your judges as at first,
your counselors as in the beginning.
Afterward you will be called
City of Righteousness, Faithful City.”|Retain restored institutions and two names.
1:27|Zion will be redeemed through justice,\nand those who return to her through righteousness.|Keep redemption and returning ambiguity noted.
1:28|But rebels and sinners will be shattered together;\nthose who abandon the **LORD** will come to an end.|Retain combined judgment and abandoning relation.
1:29|They will be ashamed of the mighty trees you desired;\nyou will blush for the gardens you chose.|Preserve third/second-person shift and cultic landscapes.
1:30|You will be like a terebinth with withering leaves,\nlike a garden without water.|Keep tree species and waterlessness.

1:31|The strong will become tinder,
and their work a spark.
Both will burn together,
with no one to put them out.|Retain worker/work linkage and unquenched fire.
2:1|The word Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem:|Preserve unusual seeing a word formula.

2:2|In days to come,
the mountain of the **LORD**’s house
will stand firm above the mountains,
raised above the hills.
All nations will stream toward it.|Keep raised mountain and uphill flowing nations.

2:3|Many peoples will come and say,
“Come, let us go up to the **LORD**’s mountain,
to the house of Jacob’s God.
He will teach us his ways,
and we will walk his paths.”
For instruction will go out from Zion,
and the **LORD**’s word from Jerusalem.|Retain collective invitation and learning/walking relation.

2:4|He will judge between the nations
and settle disputes for many peoples.
They will hammer their swords into plowshares
and their spears into pruning hooks.
Nation will not lift sword against nation;
they will no longer learn war.|Preserve instruments transformed and unlearned warfare.
2:5|House of Jacob, come!\nLet us walk in the **LORD**’s light.|Retain invitation echo and light image.

2:6|You have abandoned your people, the house of Jacob.
They are full of practices from the east,
of diviners like the Philistines;
they clasp hands with foreigners.|Retain address to God and difficult foreign practice claims.

2:7|Their land is full of silver and gold,
with no end to their treasures;
their land is full of horses,
with no end to their chariots.|Keep repeated fullness and endlessness.
2:8|Their land is full of idols.\nThey bow to the work of their hands,\nto what their own fingers have made.|Preserve hand/finger irony.
2:9|Humanity bows down; people are brought low.\nDo not forgive them.|Retain startling negative petition.
2:10|Go into the rocks; hide in the dust\nfrom the terror of the **LORD**,\nfrom the splendor of his majesty.|Keep hiding command and paired divine effects.
2:11|Humanity’s proud eyes will be lowered;\nhuman arrogance will bow.\nThe **LORD** alone will be exalted on that day.|Preserve human/divine height reversal.
2:12|For the **LORD** of hosts has a day\nagainst everything proud and lofty,\neverything raised high—it will be brought low;|Retain day against exalted things and continuation.
2:13|against all Lebanon’s cedars, tall and towering,\nand all Bashan’s oaks;|Keep two named tree regions.
2:14|against all the high mountains\nand every towering hill;|Preserve mountain/hill parallel.
2:15|against every lofty tower\nand every fortified wall;|Retain military architecture.
2:16|against all the ships of Tarshish\nand every splendid vessel.|Keep Tarshish ships, uncertain second noun noted.
2:17|Human arrogance will bow;\nhumanity’s pride will be lowered.\nThe **LORD** alone will be exalted on that day.|Match refrain with source’s altered order.
2:18|The idols will disappear completely.|Retain total disappearance.

2:20|On that day people will throw away
the silver idols and gold idols
made for them to worship—
throw them to the moles and bats—|Retain metals, animals, and unfinished action.
2:22|Stop relying on human beings,\nwhose breath is in their nostrils.\nWhat are they worth?|Retain mortal breath and valuation question.

3:1|Look! The Lord, the **LORD** of hosts,
is removing from Jerusalem and Judah
every support and supply:
all support of bread and water,|Preserve divine titles and repeated support.
3:2|warrior and soldier,\njudge and prophet,\ndiviner and elder,|Retain all six social roles.
3:3|captain of fifty and person of rank,\ncounselor, skilled craftsman,\nand expert in charms.|Keep fifty and ambiguous skilled professions.
3:4|“I will make boys their rulers;\ncapricious children will govern them.”|Retain divine appointment and instability image.

3:5|People will oppress one another,
each against a neighbor.
The young will bully the old,
the despised the honored.|Keep mutual harm and age/status reversals.
3:6|A man will seize his brother in their father’s house:\n“You have a cloak—be our leader!\nTake charge of this heap of ruins.”|Retain kin setting and absurd cloak qualification.

3:7|But that day he will protest:
“I cannot bind up your wounds!
My house has neither bread nor cloak.
Do not make me the people’s leader.”|Keep healer metaphor and refused office.
3:8|Jerusalem has stumbled; Judah has fallen.\nTheir speech and deeds oppose the **LORD**,\ndefying his glorious presence.|Render eyes of glory as presence with note.

3:9|Their faces testify against them;
like Sodom, they declare their sin without hiding it.
Woe to them!
They have brought harm on themselves.|Retain self-incrimination and explicit Sodom.
3:10|Tell the righteous it will go well:\nthey will eat the fruit of their deeds.|Keep eating moral fruit.
3:11|Woe to the wicked! It will go badly:\nwhat their hands have done will return to them.|Retain recompense and hands.

3:12|My people—children oppress them,
and women rule over them.
My people, your guides mislead you;
they swallow up the path you should walk.|Preserve gendered indictment, no silent alternate vocalization.
3:13|The **LORD** takes his stand to argue the case;\nhe rises to judge peoples.|Keep courtroom and plural peoples.

3:14|The **LORD** enters judgment
with his people’s elders and rulers:
“You have devoured the vineyard!
Your houses hold what you stole from the poor.|Retain vineyard accusation and concrete stolen goods.
3:15|What do you mean by crushing my people,\ngrinding the faces of the poor?”\ndeclares the Lord **GOD** of hosts.|Keep physical violence and divine-name typography distinction.

3:16|The **LORD** says:
“Because Zion’s daughters are proud,
walking with necks outstretched
and eyes that flirt,
taking mincing steps
and jingling their anklets,|Retain specific female display and causal continuation.
3:17|the Lord will scab the heads of Zion’s daughters;\nthe **LORD** will expose their private parts.”|Preserve humiliating bodily threat, alternative scalp noted.
3:18|On that day the Lord will remove their finery: anklets, headbands, crescent ornaments,|Retain complete adornment catalogue beginning.
3:19|earrings, bracelets, veils,|Preserve three ornaments without expansion.
3:20|headdresses, ankle chains, sashes, perfume containers, amulets,|Keep five distinct items and magical ornament.
3:21|rings and nose jewels,|Retain two jewelry locations.
3:22|fine robes, mantles, wraps, purses,|Keep four garment/accessory terms.
3:23|mirrors, linen garments, turbans, and shawls.|Preserve final four items, uncertain identifications noted.
3:25|Your men will fall by the sword,\nyour warriors in battle.|Retain address to city and deaths.
3:26|Her gates will lament and mourn;\nstripped bare, she will sit on the ground.|Preserve personified gates and devastated woman-city.

4:1|On that day seven women will seize one man and say, “We will eat our own bread and wear our own clothes. Only let us bear your name; take away our disgrace.”|Keep seven-to-one ratio and women’s stated proposal.
4:2|On that day the **LORD**’s growth will be beautiful and glorious, and the land’s fruit will be the pride and splendor of Israel’s survivors.|Keep plant/fruit parallel, branch alternative noted.
4:3|Those left in Zion, those remaining in Jerusalem, will be called holy—everyone recorded for life in Jerusalem.|Retain remnant and life register.

4:4|When the Lord has washed away the filth of Zion’s daughters and rinsed Jerusalem’s blood from her midst by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning,|Preserve washing, blood, and spirit ambiguity.

4:5|the **LORD** will create over all Mount Zion’s dwelling places and assemblies a cloud by day, smoke, and the glow of flaming fire by night. Over all the glory there will be a canopy,|Keep cloud/fire pattern and covering.
4:6|a shelter giving shade from the daytime heat, a refuge and hiding place from storm and rain.|Retain weather-specific protection.

5:1|Let me sing for my beloved
my beloved’s song about his vineyard.
My beloved had a vineyard
on a fertile hillside.|Keep singer and beloved distinct.

5:2|He dug it, cleared its stones,
and planted choice vines.
He built a tower in its midst
and cut out a winepress.
He expected grapes,
but it produced foul fruit.|Preserve preparations and failed expectation.
5:3|“Now, inhabitants of Jerusalem and people of Judah,\njudge between me and my vineyard.|Keep owner’s first-person appeal.

5:4|What more could I have done for my vineyard
that I have not done?
Why, when I expected grapes,
did it produce foul fruit?|Retain repeated fruit question.

5:5|Now I will tell you
what I will do to my vineyard:
remove its hedge, and it will be devoured;
break its wall, and it will be trampled.|Keep two removed protections and consequences.

5:6|I will make it a wasteland,
neither pruned nor hoed,
overgrown with thorns and briers.
I will command the clouds
to send no rain on it.”|Retain agricultural neglect and cloud command.

5:7|The vineyard of the **LORD** of hosts is the house of Israel;
the people of Judah are the planting he delighted in.
He expected justice—but look, bloodshed!
Righteousness—but listen, a cry!|Preserve accusation’s sound-driven contrasts in note.

5:8|Woe to those who join house to house
and add field to field,
until no room remains
and you live alone in the land!|Keep land concentration and exclusion.
5:9|The **LORD** of hosts has spoken in my hearing:\n“Surely many houses will lie desolate,\nlarge and beautiful, with no one living there.|Supply speech for in-my-ears formula.
5:10|Ten yoke of vineyard will yield one bath,\nand a homer of seed will yield an ephah.”|Preserve exact ancient quantities for note.
5:11|Woe to those who rise early to chase strong drink\nand linger late, inflamed by wine!|Keep morning/night and burning wine.

5:12|Lyre and harp, tambourine and flute,
and wine fill their feasts.
But they do not regard the **LORD**’s work
or see what his hands have done.|Retain four instruments and ignored divine work.
5:13|So my people go into exile for lack of knowledge.\nTheir honored people die of hunger;\ntheir masses are parched with thirst.|Keep exile, status contrast, hunger/thirst.

5:14|So Sheol widens its appetite
and opens its mouth without limit.
Down go Jerusalem’s splendor and crowds,
her uproar and revelers.|Preserve devouring underworld and descent.
5:15|Humanity bows down; people are brought low;\nproud eyes are lowered.|Retain repeated lowering and eyes.
5:16|But the **LORD** of hosts is exalted through justice;\nthe holy God shows himself holy through righteousness.|Keep holiness/justice linkage.
5:17|Lambs will graze as in their pasture,\nand strangers will eat among the ruins of the well-fed.|Follow strangers text, not silently lambs emendation.
5:18|Woe to those who drag guilt with cords of falsehood\nand sin as with cart ropes,|Keep hauling metaphor and differing ropes.

5:19|who say, “Let him hurry!
Let him speed his work so we can see it!
Let the Holy One of Israel’s plan come near,
let it arrive so we may know!”|Preserve mocking demand and title.
5:20|Woe to those who call evil good and good evil,\nwho turn darkness into light and light into darkness,\nwho turn bitter into sweet and sweet into bitter!|Keep three reversible pairs.
5:21|Woe to those wise in their own eyes\nand discerning in their own sight!|Retain self-assessed wisdom.
5:22|Woe to heroes at drinking wine,\nvaliant men at mixing strong drink,|Keep ironic military praise.
5:23|who acquit the wicked for a bribe\nand take the righteous person’s rights away!|Retain courtroom injustice.

5:24|As a tongue of fire eats stubble
and dry grass collapses in flame,
their root will rot
and their blossom rise like dust.
They have rejected the instruction of the **LORD** of hosts
and scorned the Holy One of Israel’s word.|Keep two combustion images and root/blossom destruction.
5:26|He will raise a signal for distant nations\nand whistle for them from the earth’s end.\nLook, they come swiftly, speedily!|Keep plural/singular collective movement and summons.

5:28|Their arrows are sharp,
all their bows drawn.
Their horses’ hooves seem like flint,
their wheels like a whirlwind.|Keep weapon and chariot similes.

5:29|Their roar is like a lion’s;
they roar like young lions.
They growl, seize prey,
and carry it off with no one to rescue it.|Retain repeated lion sounds and absent rescue.

5:30|On that day they will growl over it
like the sea’s roar.
Look toward the land:
darkness and distress!
Even the light is darkened by its clouds.|Preserve ominous land view and darkened light.
6:1|In the year King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and lifted up. The train of his robe filled the temple.|Retain dated vision and robe scale.
6:2|Seraphim stood above him. Each had six wings: with two each covered his face, with two his feet, and with two he flew.|Keep six divided into three pairs.
6:3|They called to one another:\n“Holy, holy, holy is the **LORD** of hosts!\nThe whole earth is full of his glory!”|Preserve threefold holy and antiphonal call.
6:4|The doorposts shook at the sound of the one calling, and the house filled with smoke.|Retain structural shaking and smoke.
6:5|I said, “Woe to me! I am undone. I am a man of unclean lips, living among a people of unclean lips, yet my eyes have seen the King, the **LORD** of hosts.”|Keep shared impurity and royal vision.
6:6|One of the seraphim flew to me with a glowing coal in his hand, taken from the altar with tongs.|Retain altar and tool-mediated coal.
6:7|He touched my mouth and said, “Look, this has touched your lips. Your guilt has departed; your sin is atoned for.”|Preserve physical contact and atonement term.
6:8|Then I heard the Lord’s voice: “Whom shall I send? Who will go for us?” I said, “Here I am. Send me!”|Keep singular/plural divine speech unharmonized.
6:9|He said, “Go and tell this people:\n‘Keep listening, but do not understand;\nkeep looking, but do not know.’|Retain commanded nonunderstanding.

6:10|Make this people’s heart dull,
make their ears heavy,
close their eyes,
lest they see with their eyes,
hear with their ears,
understand with their heart,
turn back, and be healed.”|Preserve hardening commission and lest force.
6:11|I asked, “How long, Lord?” He said, “Until cities lie ruined without inhabitants, houses without people, and the land lies utterly desolate;|Retain question and threefold emptiness.
6:12|until the **LORD** has sent people far away and abandoned places multiply in the land.|Keep exile and abandonment.
6:13|Even if a tenth remains, it will again be burned, like a terebinth or oak whose stump remains when felled. The holy seed is its stump.”|Retain tenth, repeated destruction, and seed/stump hope.

7:1|In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, marched up to wage war against Jerusalem, but could not overcome it.|Retain full royal relationships and failed assault.

7:2|When the house of David was told, “Aram has joined Ephraim,” the king’s heart and his people’s hearts shook like forest trees shaking in the wind.|Keep dynastic audience and shared trembling simile.

7:3|The **LORD** said to Isaiah, “Go out to meet Ahaz, you and your son Shear-jashub, at the end of the upper pool’s channel, by the road to the washer’s field.|Retain sign-child and precise meeting location.

7:4|Tell him: ‘Take care and stay calm. Do not fear; do not lose heart before these two smoking stubs of firewood—before the burning anger of Rezin and Aram and Remaliah’s son.|Keep diminishing firewood image and enemy names.
7:5|Aram, Ephraim, and Remaliah’s son have plotted harm against you, saying,|Preserve three named conspirators.
7:6|“Let us invade Judah, terrify it, and break it open for ourselves. We will install Tabeel’s son as king there.”|Retain proposed puppet ruler and invasion verbs.
7:7|But the Lord **GOD** says:\n“It will not stand.\nIt will not happen.|Keep two denials and divine-name distinction.

7:8|Aram’s head is Damascus,
and Damascus’s head is Rezin.
Within sixty-five years
Ephraim will be shattered, no longer a people.|Retain political hierarchy and exact interval.

7:9|Ephraim’s head is Samaria,
and Samaria’s head is Remaliah’s son.
If you do not stand firm in faith,
you will not stand firm at all.”’”|Preserve faith/firmness wordplay in English.
7:10|The **LORD** spoke to Ahaz again:|Retain renewed divine address.

7:11|“Ask the **LORD** your God for a sign—make your request as deep as you wish or as high as the heights.”|Retain the pointed request verb and extreme depth/height; note the alternative repointing as Sheol.
7:12|Ahaz answered, “I will not ask. I will not put the **LORD** to the test.”|Preserve refusal and stated reason.
7:13|Isaiah said, “Listen, house of David! Is it not enough to weary people? Must you weary my God too?|Clarify speaker and retain my-God shift.

7:14|Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Look, the young woman is pregnant and will bear a son. And you will name him Immanuel.|Follow almah and present pregnancy; preserve the shift to second-person feminine naming, documenting alternatives.
7:15|He will eat curds and honey when he knows to reject evil and choose good.|Retain food and moral discernment timing.
7:16|Before the boy knows to reject evil and choose good, the land whose two kings terrify you will be abandoned.|Keep repeated developmental limit and two kings.

7:17|The **LORD** will bring upon you, your people, and your father’s house days unlike any since Ephraim separated from Judah—the king of Assyria!”|Retain three targets and delayed Assyria disclosure.
7:18|On that day the **LORD** will whistle for flies from the farthest channels of Egypt and bees from Assyria.|Keep insects, locations, and whistle.
7:19|They will all come and settle in steep ravines, rock crevices, every thornbush, and every watering place.|Preserve four occupied habitats.

7:20|On that day the Lord will use a razor hired beyond the River—the king of Assyria—to shave the head and the hair of the legs, and sweep away the beard as well.|Keep humiliating shaving and legs euphemism note.
7:21|On that day a person will keep alive one young cow and two sheep.|Preserve one/two remnant livestock.
7:22|Their abundant milk will provide curds to eat. Everyone left in the land will eat curds and honey.|Keep abundance within devastated-land setting.
7:23|On that day every place where a thousand vines stood, worth a thousand pieces of silver, will become thorns and briers.|Retain paired thousands and land regression.
7:24|People will go there with bow and arrows, for the whole land will be thorns and briers.|Keep hunting equipment and repeated overgrowth.

7:25|As for all the hills once worked with a hoe, you will not go there for fear of thorns and briers. They will become places for cattle to roam and sheep to trample.|Choose fear-caused avoidance, retaining alternative syntax in note.
8:1|The **LORD** said to me, “Take a large tablet and write on it with an ordinary stylus: ‘For Maher-shalal-hash-baz.’”|Preserve sign’s material, script, and name.
8:2|“I will call reliable witnesses for myself: Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah.”|Retain first-person divine witness statement.
8:3|I went to the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. The **LORD** said to me, “Name him Maher-shalal-hash-baz.|Keep prophetess title and conception sequence.
8:4|Before the boy knows how to say ‘My father’ or ‘My mother,’ Damascus’s wealth and Samaria’s plunder will be carried before the king of Assyria.”|Retain two infant words and two spoils.
8:5|The **LORD** spoke to me again:|Keep renewed message formula.
8:6|“Because this people has rejected\nthe gently flowing waters of Shiloah\nand rejoices over Rezin and Remaliah’s son,|Retain rejoicing reading, not silently melt-in-fear emendation.

8:7|the Lord is bringing against them
the River’s mighty, surging waters—
the king of Assyria in all his glory.
It will rise over every channel
and overflow every bank.|Preserve explicit interpretation within river metaphor.

8:8|It will sweep into Judah, flooding through,
reaching up to the neck.
Its outspread wings will fill your land’s breadth,
Immanuel.”|Keep river-to-wing shift and named addressee.

8:9|Rage, peoples, and be shattered!
Listen, all distant lands!
Prepare for battle—and be shattered!
Prepare for battle—and be shattered!|Retain repeated imperatives and uncertain opening verb.
8:10|Devise a plan—it will be broken.\nSpeak a word—it will not stand,\nfor God is with us.|Preserve Immanuel meaning as sentence.
8:11|The **LORD** spoke to me with his hand strong upon me, warning me not to walk in this people’s way:|Keep forceful hand and path warning.

8:12|“Do not call everything a conspiracy
that this people calls a conspiracy.
Do not fear what they fear
or be terrified.|Retain conspiracy repetition and fear pair.
8:13|The **LORD** of hosts—regard him as holy.\nLet him be your fear,\nlet him be your terror.|Keep holiness and doubled fear object.

8:14|He will become a sanctuary,
yet a stone to strike against,
a rock to stumble over,
for both houses of Israel;
a trap and snare for Jerusalem’s inhabitants.|Preserve sanctuary/stumbling tension and two houses.
8:15|Many will stumble over them,\nfall and break,\nbe snared and caught.”|Keep five linked consequences.
8:16|Bind up the testimony;\nseal the instruction among my disciples.|Retain transmission commands and learners.
8:17|I will wait for the **LORD**,\nwho hides his face from the house of Jacob.\nI will hope in him.|Keep hope despite hidden face.
8:18|Here I am, with the children the **LORD** has given me, as signs and wonders in Israel from the **LORD** of hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.|Retain family signs and two divine references.

8:19|When they tell you, “Consult the mediums and spiritists who chirp and mutter,” should not a people consult its God? Should the dead be consulted for the living?|Keep sounds and living/dead question.
8:20|To the instruction and the testimony! If they do not speak according to this word, there is no dawn for them.|Retain abrupt summons and dawn image, syntax noted.

8:21|They will pass through the land distressed and hungry. When hunger overtakes them, they will rage and curse their king and their God. They will turn their faces upward,|Keep hunger-to-curse sequence and upward look.
8:22|then look toward the earth: distress and darkness, oppressive gloom! They will be driven into deep darkness.|Preserve doubled direction and unrelieved darkness.

9:1|Yet there will be no gloom for the land in anguish. In the former time he brought the land of Zebulun and Naphtali into contempt; in the latter he has honored the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.|Map source8:23; retain geographic sweep and temporal contrast.
9:2|The people walking in darkness have seen a great light;\nlight has shone on those dwelling in a land of deep shadow.|Keep perfect vision and parallel darkness/light.

9:3|You have multiplied the nation
and increased its joy.
They rejoice before you
as at harvest,
as people exult when dividing plunder.|Follow joy read form, record negative written alternative.

9:4|For the yoke that burdened them,
the bar across their shoulders,
the rod of their oppressor—
you have shattered them as on the day of Midian.|Preserve three oppression implements and historical allusion.
9:5|Every boot that tramped in battle\nand every garment rolled in blood\nwill be burned, fuel for the fire.|Retain bloody military objects and burning.

9:6|For a child has been born for us,
a son has been given to us.
Authority rests on his shoulder,
and his name is called
Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God,
Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.|Preserve child/son, shoulder, full titles without extra doctrinal gloss.

9:7|His authority will increase,
and peace will have no end,
on David’s throne and over his kingdom,
establishing and upholding it
with justice and righteousness
